chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of a child for his parent and the parent for his child and the brother for his brother, so he said, 'It is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child for their parent or a brother for his brother valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on testimonies, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the general permissibility of testimony between parents and children, as well as siblings. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that the potential bias inherent in close familial ties does not invalidate their testimony, distinguishing it from cases where kinship might imply greater partiality. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the flexibility of evidentiary rules regarding immediate family members in legal disputes.
